title: Repo and Reverse Repo Agreements

source.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

summary: This New York Fed page provides an overview of how the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) authorized Open Market Trading Desk conducts repo and reverse repo operations to implement monetary policy and maintain the federal funds rate within the target range. The page describes the operational framework for Overnight Reverse Repo (ON RRP) operations, which provide a floor under overnight rates, and Standing Repo (SRP) operations, which provide a ceiling on money market rates.
key_points: The Desk conducts repo transactions (purchasing securities with agreement to resell) to increase reserve balances and reverse repo transactions (selling securities with agreement to repurchase) to reduce reserve balances.
ON RRP operations limit downward pressure on overnight rates by offering an alternative investment for money market investors when rates fall below IORB.
Standing repo operations limit upward pressure on overnight rates and provide a ceiling on money market rates.
ON RRP counterparties include primary dealers, banks, money market mutual funds, and government sponsored enterprises; eligible collateral is U.S. Treasury securities.
SRP counterparties include primary dealers and eligible depository institutions; eligible collateral includes Treasury, agency debt, and agency mortgage-backed securities.
Recent announcements referenced on the page include April 3, 2026 (Open Market Desk Operations) and March 12, 2026 (Repurchase Agreement Small Value Exercise).
why_it_matters: This source explains the fundamental market structure tools the Fed uses to control short-term interest rates. Understanding repo and reverse repo operations is essential for comprehending how monetary policy is transmitted to financial markets and how the Fed maintains control of the fed funds rate corridor.
market_structure_context: This page documents the Fed's monetary policy implementation framework, specifically the operational tools (ON RRP and SRP) that maintain the fed funds rate within the FOMC's target range. The ON RRP provides a floor under overnight rates while SRP provides a ceiling, together forming the corridor for short-term rates.
